label: sparse near-threshold feature on d/a tokens or after z (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse (0.016% of steps) and almost all activations sit just above threshold (min about 0.5 of max, median 0.117 vs max 0.196). Enriched contexts: input tok d (12x) or a (8x); previous input z (10x), especially orig(3)=z at t=4 in sequences starting with d or a (the top examples); copy-phase steps right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1) or near the end of the copy (to_go<=2) where the input is d/a; and sequences with no digits. It never fires at t=0-2 or on the delimiter step. Every predicate tried has precision under 9%: these token contexts are common and the feature fires on only a tiny, unpredictable subset of them. The best F1 was about 0.09 (t=4, orig(3)=z, first token d/a). A broad disjunction (prev z at t>=3, or copy-phase input d/a) reaches 0.81 recall at 0.25% precision. Magnitude is nearly flat, and the larger values are concentrated in the t=4-after-z case.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=d (+4.87), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+4.69), phase=2 & out_tok=q (+4.21), phase=2 & out_tok=a (+3.83), prev_tok=z (+3.69), phase=2 & out_tok=d (+3.23). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-4.42), prev3_tok=- (-3.84), prev2_tok=a (-2.24).
